budget_items.what_was_said: The chair announced a surplus recently discovered in the FY25 school budget, calling it too large to be a routine cushion and saying it meant students went without unnecessarily.
The chair said the district normally runs a much smaller surplus used to cover emergencies and end-of-year budget gaps.
The business manager moved money out of the dues/fees athletic expense account into the special detail athletic events account to zero out a negative balance.

budget_items.topic: Business manager salary to school stipends transfer
budget_items.what_was_said: Money was moved from the business manager salary account into school stipends because stipend spending had exceeded budget.
The stipend account was described as revised upward after being exceeded, with committee members asking whether more clubs ran than were budgeted.
Funds were moved out of maintenance of buildings to cover negative balances in sewage disposal, electricity, and telephone accounts for FY25.
The business manager said the FY26 electricity line was increased after FY25 came in over budget.

budget_items.topic: Computers purchase and lease line item
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked why roughly $95,000 budgeted for computers was left unspent; the business manager said the FY26 line was reduced because so much went unspent.
Members asked why paraprofessional lines ran a large surplus; staff attributed it to turnover and unfilled positions and possible double-budgeting against the IDEA grant.

The business manager said the IDEA federal special education grant covered a large amount in salaries, raising the question of whether paraprofessionals were budgeted in both the grant and the general fund.
The business manager stated the total warrant amount for the period covering mid-June through late August 2025.
The superintendent reported total enrollment across the district this fall, including students in the ACE program.

budget_items.topic: K-8 literacy coach position funded by Student Opportunity Act grant
budget_items.what_was_said: A newly filled literacy coach position, previously eliminated in the FY26 budget, is being paid for through a one-year extension of the district's Student Opportunity Act grant, awarded competitively to 10 of 21 applicant districts.

budget_items.topic: Additional Chapter 70 funds for fall town meeting warrant
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said extra Chapter 70 money had been allocated in the spring process and asked about placing it on the fall town meeting warrant for the schools; the town manager and superintendent were scheduling a meeting to discuss it.
Members discussed the idea of a town stabilization fund, funded by annual school surplus remittances, to absorb the cost shock of new out-of-district special education placements moving into town.
The business manager gave the available/unspent budget balances remaining at year end for FY22 through FY24 to show this year's remittance was unusually large by comparison.
The business manager estimated the average amount left on the table over the prior three years compared to his typical past experience elsewhere.

budget_items.topic: Cost drivers behind the FY25 comparison
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager cited special education tuition and utilities as major cost increases identified in his cost comparison work.

budget_items.topic: FY25 override-year budget cuts vs. surplus
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled a contentious fight over roughly $500,000 in free cash during the FY25 budget process, contrasting it with the surplus now being returned, including cuts to high school paraprofessionals, a PE teacher, two vice principals, and an athletic director.
The business manager cited a large rise in health insurance costs as another driver identified in the cost comparison.

budget_items.topic: Alternative uses for the surplus, raised in public comment
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident and select board member noted the surplus could have covered the fire department's requested fourth shift and referenced a prior athletic revolving fund deficit and a copier line-item transfer.

budget_items.topic: Surplus as a share of the override
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said the surplus amounted to a stated share of the override passed for that fiscal year, raising the question of whether the override amount or its management was the real problem.

budget_items.topic: Capital plan funding and borrowing limits
budget_items.what_was_said: The capital planning committee representative described capital funding as a mix of free cash, a raise-and-appropriate levy contribution, and possible future borrowing (regular borrowing or a debt exclusion) for large projects like the track and field, noting a policy limit on non-excluded debt service as a share of the total budget.

minutes.headline: District disclosed a roughly $582,000 unspent FY25 school surplus that went unnoticed and unbudgeted for.
minutes.summary: The School Committee's meeting centered on a newly discovered FY25 budget surplus of roughly $582,000 (about 2% of the budget), far above the district's normal cushion, which the chair and later the business manager attributed to poor financial oversight rather than known wrongdoing. The committee approved FY25 line-item transfers and a warrant, heard the superintendent's and building principals' start-of-year reports (including the first-day fire at the middle/high school), reviewed an FY27 budget timeline, and discussed a possible best-practices/forensic audit, a stabilization fund for out-of-district special education placements, and extra Chapter 70 money for a fall town meeting warrant article; several residents used public comment to press for accountability and clearer FY25-vs-FY26 budget transparency.

what_happened.line: The chair disclosed a school budget surplus described as far larger than the district's normal cushion, calling it unbudgeted and unnoticed.
The committee voted to approve five FY25 line-item transfers, shifting money between accounts including athletics, stipends, and building maintenance to cover shortfalls.
Members and the business manager questioned whether paraprofessional positions were funded both in the general fund and against a federal special education grant.
Rather than vote, the committee put off a decision on a forensic or best-practices audit of FY25 and FY26 finances, asking the chair to bring back scope and possible RFP language next meeting.
The committee voted to approve a proposed FY27 budget development timeline.

why_it_matters: How the surplus was found and explained bears on trust in the budget process residents rely on when they vote on overrides and town meeting articles.
Whether paraprofessional pay was counted twice, once in the district budget and once in a federal grant, could change the real size of the special education budget line taxpayers fund.
A possible audit and a proposed reserve fund for out-of-district special education placements would, if pursued, show up as future warrant articles at town meeting.
watch_next: Next School Committee meeting: audit scope and draft RFP language
Tri-board agenda item on an out-of-district placement stabilization fund

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the core actions of the meeting: both non-procedural votes, three of the five FY25 line-item transfers, the enrollment figure, and most of the dollar figures raised in public comment (the 61% override share, the $470K/$100K/$19K public-comment figures, the $500,000 cuts figure) match across both. The main things worth checking are two dollar amounts that don't reconcile cleanly (the athletic dues/fees transfer and the warrant total), two committee members (Gilman, Yapp) who appear in the official roll call and as seconding motions but are entirely absent from our attendee list, and several decisions/action items (the emergency-contact policy referral, the tri-board stabilization-fund agenda item, the forensic-audit follow-up plan) that our minutes capture but the official minutes never mention.
